title: Move a bulky wall-wart adapter to the end outlet of a crowded power strip so a fourth cord can plug in
instruction: Plug the black cord on the right into the power strip so all four cords end up plugged in; keep the blue and grey plugs connected throughout, though you may unplug and move the white adapter.
context: On a standard longitudinal household or office power strip, plugging a vertical AC wall-wart adapter into an interior socket lets its overhanging case cover the neighbouring empty socket. When the strip is free-standing on a desk and already supplies two connected cords that must not be interrupted, plugging in a fourth cord requires steadying the strip with one hand while temporarily unplugging the bulky adapter with the other, moving the adapter one socket over to the end outlet so its body hangs harmlessly past the end of the strip, and seating both the moved adapter and the new cord flush with no exposed blades.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top z = 0). Strip mat: fixed charcoal rubber, 16.0 x 28.0 x 0.4 cm at (24.5, -2.0), fitted with a 0.45 cm alignment frame (fabricate.py: strip_cleat_frame.stl). Cord mat: fixed olive-slate rubber, 14.0 x 9.0 x 0.4 cm at (24.5, -18.5). Power strip: an unwired CyberPower CSB404 4-outlet longitudinal NEMA 5-15R strip ($7.99, ASIN B004K1YG22; ivory ABS housing 5.0 cm along x by 21.4 cm along y from y_rel = -8.6 to +12.8 cm by 3.5 cm tall, 380 +/- 10 g on the strip mat at (24.5, -2.0), red rocker bezel at y_rel = +8.4 cm; 4 longitudinal outlets at 3.20 cm pitch: Outlet 1 at y_rel = +3.6 cm, Outlet 2 at +0.4 cm, Outlet 3 at -2.8 cm, end Outlet 4 at -6.0 cm, each with polarized blade slots at x_rel = +/-0.635 cm, y_slot = y_outlet + 0.52 cm and ground bore at x_rel = 0.0, y_slot = y_outlet - 0.67 cm). Its integral 1.2 m (4 ft) ivory 14 AWG SJT supply cord exits the +y end at (24.5, +11.3), turns +x through an adhesive desk clip at (35.0, +11.4), and drops off the +x desk edge (x = +50 cm) with its NEMA 5-15P plug left unplugged on the floor. Pre-seated cords: Outlet 1 holds a Monoprice 107673 1.8 m (6 ft) blue 18 AWG SVT NEMA 5-15P to IEC C13 cord (2.8 x 2.4 x 2.8 cm plug, 48 g) and Outlet 2 holds a StarTech PXT101 1.8 m grey 18 AWG SJT NEMA 5-15P to IEC C13 cord (48 g); both cords exit +x through a dual desk clip at (36.0, 0.0) off the +x desk edge with their IEC C13 ends taped unweighted to the front desk leg (15 cm desk slack). Outlet 3 holds a white TP-Link T120150-2B1 12V 1.5A 2-prong wall-wart adapter ($9.99; 3.4 x 6.2 x 3.8 cm with a 3.9 x 3.6 x 0.3 cm top bezel, 105 +/- 5 g; NEMA 1-15P blades 1.4 cm inside its +y face so its 4.8 cm -y overhang spans y_rel = -7.6 to -1.4 cm, covering Outlet 4); its 1.5 m black 22 AWG DC barrel cord exits +x in a loose 22 cm slack loop through a clip at (36.0, -8.6) off the +x edge (barrel end taped to the front leg). Loose black cord: a Monoprice 105278 1.8 m black 18 AWG SVT NEMA 5-15P to IEC C13 cord (3.4 x 2.4 x 3.8 cm plug with 3.9 x 2.4 x 0.3 cm pull-cap, 1.45 cm blades, 1.60 cm ground pin, 64 g), staged prongs-down at (24.5, -18.5) on fabricate.py: plug_cord_cradle.stl (ground pin 0.25 cm clear of mat); its cord exits +x in a loose 35 cm slack loop through a clip at (38.0, -18.0) off the +x edge (IEC C13 end taped to the front leg). Both arms start at READY.
scoring: The trial's score is evaluated at its final step (SCORE_OVER = end; zero permanent positive latches). Permanent 0.0 failure latches: (a) existing_unplugged: either connected appliance plug (Outlet 1 blue plug or Outlet 2 grey plug) lifts > 0.15 cm (> 1.5 mm, exposing blade metal) off the strip top face or leaves its socket at any step; (b) strip_tipped: the free-standing power strip tilts > 25.0 deg, drifts > 6.0 cm from (24.5, -2.0), or drops off the table. Let strip_undisturbed hold when the power strip rests upright (tilt <= 8.0 deg) within <= 3.0 cm of (24.5, -2.0). Let plug_in_outlet(plug, k) hold when a plug sits coaxially in Outlet k with |dx|, |dy| <= 0.45 cm, flush face gap between -0.15 cm and +0.15 cm of the +3.5 cm strip top face (<= 1.5 mm gap, leaving zero exposed brass blade metal), relative tilt <= 5.0 deg, and relative yaw <= 8.0 deg. End-step tiers (given no failure latched and strip_undisturbed + Outlet 1 & Outlet 2 still seated <= 1.5 mm): 1.00 when the white adapter is seated flush (<= 1.5 mm, no exposed blades) in end Outlet 4 (overhanging 2.2 cm past the -8.6 cm strip end), the black cord plug is seated flush (<= 1.5 mm, no exposed blades) in Outlet 3, every finger pad of both arms is >= 3.0 cm clear of the power strip, adapter and black plug, and strip, adapter and black-plug linear speeds stay < 0.8 cm/s continuously over the final 1.0 s (20 steps at 20 Hz); 0.75 when all four plugs (1, 2, black plug in 3, white adapter in 4) sit seated <= 1.5 mm on strip_undisturbed before >= 3.0 cm hand clearance or 1.0 s stillness; 0.50 when the white adapter sits seated <= 1.5 mm in end Outlet 4 (uncovering Outlet 3) while the black plug is not yet seated <= 1.5 mm in Outlet 3; 0.25 when the white adapter has been pulled clear of Outlet 3 (> 2.2 cm laterally or > 1.8 cm vertically) without yet seating <= 1.5 mm in Outlet 4 (or if the black plug took Outlet 3 leaving the adapter unseated); 0.00 otherwise. Real trial post-run checks, in order (single 1.5 mm criterion throughout): (1) Connected-plug & strip check (from trial video + ruler): if Outlet 1 (blue) or Outlet 2 (grey) ever visibly lifted to expose blade metal (> 1.5 mm) during the trial, or if the strip tilted > 25 deg or slid > 6 cm (or ends > 3 cm off mark / > 8 deg tilted), score 0. (2) Zero-exposed-blade 1.5 mm no-go feeler & stillness check: test all four plugs — Outlet 1 (blue), Outlet 2 (grey), Outlet 3 (black), and end Outlet 4 (white adapter overhanging the -y end) — around their perimeter with the 1.5 mm no-go gauge (fabricate.py: feeler_gauge_1p5mm.stl) and inspect horizontally at strip-face level: a plug counts as seated iff the 1.5 mm feeler cannot enter between plug face and strip face, zero brass blade metal is visible, and yaw/tilt are <= 8 deg / <= 5 deg. If all four pass and video confirms >= 3.0 cm hand clearance and zero motion over the final 1.0 s, score 1.0 (0.75 before release/stillness; 0.50 if Outlets 1, 2 and adapter in 4 pass while black plug does not; 0.25 if Outlets 1 and 2 pass and Outlet 3 was cleared without seating adapter <= 1.5 mm in 4; 0 otherwise).
reset_notes: Between trials (< 20 s): keep the strip's 1.2 m supply plug disconnected on the floor; hold the strip down, pull the black plug from Outlet 3, set it prongs-down onto plug_cord_cradle.stl at (24.5, -18.5) and dress its 35 cm +x slack loop to the (38.0, -18.0) clip; move the white TP-Link adapter from Outlet 4 back into Outlet 3 (<= 1.5 mm feeler check) with its 22 cm DC loop to (36.0, -8.6); verify Outlets 1 & 2 pass the 1.5 mm feeler and align the strip in strip_cleat_frame.stl.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with 240 Hz convex-hull PhysX contact. All 4 longitudinal NEMA 5-15R outlets have true 3-cavity blade slots and ground bores; plugs carry 14.5 mm tapered blades and 16.0 mm ground pins (~3.2 mm per-side clearance for rigid insertion vs ~15-25 N real spring-clip retention; both enforce the same <=1.5 mm zero-exposed-blade check). Off-workspace PVC cord slack beyond the rigid +x boots is shown as static routed guides (<0.2 N slack load); mains power is unenergized.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (600 steps: reaches right arm to the black plug on the cradle without moving the white adapter in Outlet 3); demo: 1.0 (seed=0 in 469 steps, seed=1: 1.0, <=1.5 mm seating); checks: unplug_existing 0.00, unplug_wart_only 0.25, move_wart_only 0.50
